correctness.rationale: The constant kernel feature cancels for simplex weights; the error is the Euclidean center-to-hull distance. On a miss the unique gap of length pi+delta leaves a short occupied arc; its closing chord attains distance sin(delta/2). For an anchor in the direction of increasing angle the tail event forces all other points into the arc of mass 1/2 minus the displayed integral. Choices of anchor index are disjoint. In cumulative-mass coordinates, conditional on a miss and the anchor, the excess mass of the exceptional gap has survival (1-2m)^(N-1) on [0,1/2], independent of the anchor. Thus the scaled excess mass has rate 2, and rescaling back from mass to angle and distance gives rate 4f(theta). The positive minimum of f bounds the conditional scaled-distance tail by exp(-2 min(f) t), allowing integration against p t^(p-1) for every fixed p>0. Multiplying by N/2^(N-1) gives the stated normalization; strict Jensen and the reciprocal integral for the cosine density give the last claims.
residual_risks: The increasing-angle orientation in the integral is counterclockwise in the usual Cartesian convention. The conditional density f holds for either directed gap anchor, as the half-circle mass is 1/2 from either endpoint. The scalar law is unaffected.
Continuous angles exclude positive-threshold atoms and coincident samples, including for N=2. The asymptotics are pointwise in the fixed positive density, not uniform as its minimum approaches zero.

value.rationale: Separating miss frequency from conditional loss is scientifically useful, but the frozen result recasts the existing stronger clearance analysis. Converting the known angular law by the elementary chord identity and inserting a cosine into the known moment functional are routine specializations rather than a new quadrature invariant or a new optimization principle.
residual_risks: This does not assess more general kernels, a genuinely new sampling law, or algorithmic weight selection.
